prompt_text: Some people believe that unpaid community service should be a compulsory part of high school programmes. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay_text:
Nowadays many people say high school students must do unpaid community service. In my opinion, I disagree with this because students have too much study and no time.

First, students nowadays very busy with school homework and exam. If they must do community work like clean park or help old people, they will feel very tire and cannot get good score in test. For example, my brother study until midnight every day, he have no free time for other things.

Second, doing work without money is not fair. Student need relax on weekend. Forcing student do this is make them hate community service instead of like it.

In conclusion, I think high school should not make community service compulsory. Students should focus on their study and do volunteer only when they want.

prompt_text: In many countries, more and more people are choosing to live alone. What are the causes of this, and is it a positive or negative development?
essay_text:
Today many people want living alone in many country. There is many reason for this and I think it have both good and bad side.

One reason is people want freedom. When live alone, they can do everything they want without family tell them what to do. Also, economy is better now so young people can afford rent small apartment by themself.

However, living alone has bad problem. People can feel lonely and when they sick, nobody take care. In my country, family is very important so live alone make family relationship become weak.

To sum up, living alone is increasing because freedom and money, but it has negative effect on social life.

prompt_text: Governments should spend money on railways rather than roads. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay_text:
In modern society, transportation is a major concern for many governments. Some individuals believe that public funds should be invested primarily in railways rather than road networks. Personally, I partly agree with this view because while railways are environmentally friendly, road systems are still indispensable for daily commuting.

On the one hand, investing in trains and subways can significantly reduce traffic congestion and carbon emissions. Trains can carry hundreds of passengers simultaneously, which helps decrease the number of private cars on the street. For instance, cities with advanced metro systems like Tokyo have cleaner air and fewer traffic jams.

On the other hand, roads provide unmatched flexibility that railways cannot offer. Buses, delivery trucks, and private vehicles require roads to reach remote areas and deliver goods door-to-door. If a government neglects road maintenance, rural communities will suffer severe economic isolation.

In conclusion, although expanding railway networks is vital for sustainable development, governments should allocate resources equitably between rail and road infrastructure to ensure balanced transportation.

prompt_text: Some people think that university students should pay the full cost of their tuition, while others believe that the government should fund higher education. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
essay_text:
The funding of higher education is a controversial topic worldwide. While some people argue that university students should bear the entire expense of their tertiary studies, others advocate that governments should fully subsidize higher education. In this essay, I will examine both perspectives before presenting my personal stance.

Proponents of self-funded tuition argue that university graduates usually secure higher-paying jobs compared to those with only secondary education. Therefore, it is reasonable that individuals invest in their own future rather than burdening taxpayers. Furthermore, when students pay for their tuition, they tend to be more committed and study harder to maximize their investment.

Conversely, supporters of free university education emphasize equal opportunity and national development. If higher education is completely funded by the state, talented students from underprivileged backgrounds can pursue degrees without financial barriers. Consequently, the nation benefits from a highly educated workforce, fostering innovation and economic growth.

In my opinion, a hybrid model is the most practical solution. Governments should provide generous scholarships and subsidies for essential fields like healthcare and engineering, while students can contribute a moderate tuition fee supported by interest-free student loans.

prompt_text: The increase in the production of consumer goods results in damage to the natural environment. What are the causes of this, and what measures can be taken to solve the problem?
essay_text:
The exponential surge in global consumer goods manufacturing has undeniably inflicted severe degradation on our natural ecosystems. This essay explores the primary drivers behind this environmental crisis, namely industrial pollution and disposable consumer culture, before proposing actionable remedies involving green manufacturing standards and consumer education.

To begin with, the mass manufacturing of everyday products requires substantial amounts of natural resources, including fossil fuels, minerals, and timber. Factories emit hazardous greenhouse gases and discharge toxic effluents into nearby water bodies during production cycles. Furthermore, the rise of planned obsolescence and fast fashion has fostered a throwaway mindset, leading to monumental quantities of non-biodegradable waste in landfills and oceans.

To alleviate these detrimental impacts, concerted efforts from both governments and industrial leaders are essential. Firstly, legislative authorities should enforce stringent carbon taxation and reward corporations that transition to renewable energy and closed-loop recycling mechanisms. Secondly, public awareness campaigns should encourage sustainable consumption habits, such as purchasing durable products and participating in circular economy initiatives.

In conclusion, the environmental toll of unchecked industrial production is a pressing global challenge. Nevertheless, through strict governmental regulation and conscientious consumer behavior, economic productivity can be harmonized with environmental preservation.

prompt_text: Some people think that artificial intelligence will replace human workers in the future. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay_text:
The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has sparked widespread debate regarding the future of the global labor market. While many experts predict that intelligent machines will inevitably displace human workers across various sectors, I believe that AI will primarily automate routine tasks while creating novel opportunities requiring uniquely human attributes.

Undeniably, automated systems and generative models possess superior processing speed and accuracy when performing repetitive or data-intensive duties. Occupations such as data entry, automated manufacturing, and basic customer service are increasingly being taken over by AI agents. This technological shift allows businesses to reduce operational overheads and eliminate human errors.

However, it is overly pessimistic to claim that human labor will become obsolete. Occupations requiring emotional intelligence, critical ethical judgment, and authentic artistic creativity remain firmly beyond the scope of algorithmic computation. For instance, healthcare professionals, psychological counselors, and high-level strategists must navigate intricate human emotions and moral dilemmas that machines cannot comprehend. Moreover, technological revolutions historically create entirely new job categories, such as AI prompt engineers and machine learning ethicists.

In conclusion, although artificial intelligence will fundamentally disrupt conventional employment paradigms, it is more likely to function as a collaborative tool that augments human capability rather than causing widespread human obsolescence.

prompt_text: In many cities around the world, historical buildings are being replaced by modern skyscrapers. Do the advantages of this trend outweigh the disadvantages?
essay_text:
The architectural landscape of major metropolitan areas has undergone a profound transformation in recent decades, characterized by the demolition of historical edifices to erect contemporary skyscrapers. While this modernization facilitates urban densification and economic expansion, I firmly contend that the erosion of cultural heritage and architectural identity represents an overriding disadvantage.

On the one hand, the proliferation of high-rise commercial and residential towers offers undeniable pragmatic benefits for densely populated cities. Modern high-rises optimize land utilization by providing substantial floor space within compact urban footprints, accommodating corporate headquarters and mitigating housing shortages. Furthermore, contemporary buildings are engineered with energy-efficient HVAC systems and superior seismic resilience, fostering safer and more sustainable urban environments.

On the other hand, historical buildings serve as tangible embodiments of a nation's cultural lineage and historical memory. The systematic eradication of heritage structures homogenizes urban aesthetics, rendering cosmopolitan cities indistinguishable and depriving citizens of their collective identity. Moreover, historical districts function as major catalysts for international tourism, generating vital revenue and employment that often surpass the transient economic yields of modern office developments. Preserving architectural heritage alongside prudent urban renewal is therefore essential.

In conclusion, although modern skyscrapers satisfy critical demographic and logistical imperatives, they should not be constructed at the expense of architectural heritage. The cultural and aesthetic impoverishment resulting from the loss of historic landmarks far outweighs the utilitarian merits of unrestricted high-rise redevelopment.

prompt_text: Some people believe that international sporting events promote peace between nations, while others think they cause conflict. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
essay_text:
International athletic spectacles, such as the Olympic Games and the FIFA World Cup, capture global attention and evoke intense passions. While some commentators argue that these global contests exacerbate geopolitical tensions and foster virulent nationalism, I maintain that their overarching capacity to cultivate intercultural empathy and diplomatic goodwill renders them potent instruments for international peace.

Critics of international sporting tournaments often point to instances where athletic rivalry degenerates into political hostility. Extreme partisan allegiance can amplify chauvinistic sentiments, leading to confrontations between opposing supporters or diplomatic boycotts orchestrated by rival nations. For example, during the Cold War era, reciprocal boycotts of the 1980 Moscow and 1984 Los Angeles Olympics exemplified how athletic platforms could be weaponized for ideological confrontation.

Nevertheless, the unifying potential of international sport far transcends its occasional politicization. Such events provide a neutral arena where athletes from divergent socio-political backgrounds interact with mutual respect, demonstrating universal human excellence. Furthermore, these tournaments foster grassroots cultural diplomacy, as hundreds of thousands of international spectators converge, dismantle entrenched stereotypes, and forge cross-cultural friendships. History demonstrates that sporting exchanges, such as 'Ping-Pong Diplomacy' between the United States and China, have repeatedly served as precursors to formal geopolitical rapprochement.

In conclusion, although the heightened emotional stakes of international competition can occasionally mirror existing political frictions, the intrinsic ethos of fair play and global camaraderie makes international sporting events an invaluable catalyst for peace and mutual understanding.

prompt_text: Scientific research should be carried out and controlled by private companies rather than governments. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay_text:
The governance and stewardship of scientific inquiry constitute a pivotal determinant of societal trajectory. While private enterprise unquestionably contributes substantial capital and commercial agility to research and development, I strongly refute the assertion that scientific exploration should be predominantly conducted and monopolized by corporate entities. Instead, state oversight and public funding remain imperative to safeguard scientific integrity, ethical standards, and equitable public accessibility.

Advocates of corporate-led research frequently cite the dynamism and financial resourcefulness inherent in the private sector. Driven by market imperatives and profit motives, corporations often expedite the translation of theoretical breakthroughs into scalable consumer products, as evidenced by the rapid synthesis and distribution of cutting-edge pharmaceuticals and consumer electronics. Moreover, private capital mitigates bureaucratic inertia, enabling agile pivot strategies in competitive technological frontiers such as quantum computing.

Nevertheless, subordinating scientific endeavors entirely to the hegemony of private enterprise entails grave structural hazards. Commercial entities are fundamentally beholden to shareholder value, creating an intrinsic bias toward commercially lucrative applications while chronically underfunding foundational, blue-skies research that lacks immediate monetizability. Furthermore, corporate proprietary interests often lead to restrictive patenting regimes and data sequestering, thereby stifling academic cross-pollination and restricting impoverished populations from accessing life-saving innovations, notably essential medicines. Crucially, state-funded research institutions operate under mandates of public interest, ensuring rigorous ethical scrutiny over sensitive domains such as genetic engineering and artificial intelligence.

In conclusion, while public-private partnerships can synergistically accelerate technological deployment, the overarching trajectory, ethical boundaries, and foundational funding of scientific research must remain anchored within the democratic purview of governmental institutions.

prompt_text: In the modern world, the discipline of philosophy is often seen as obsolete compared to science and technology. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this view?
essay_text:
In an era characterized by relentless technological disruption and empirical pragmatism, philosophical inquiry is frequently dismissed as an archaic, purely academic abstraction. However, I vehemently reject the notion that philosophy has been rendered obsolete; on the contrary, as humanity grapples with unprecedented technological power, philosophical frameworks are more indispensable than ever in guiding empirical advancements toward humane and ethical ends.

It is undeniable that empirical sciences and engineering disciplines yield tangible, quantifiable advancements that directly elevate living standards. From renewable energy grids to biomedical breakthroughs, scientific methodology provides the instrumental mechanisms required to solve existential physical dilemmas. Consequently, in utilitarian economic models that prioritize immediate return on investment, speculative philosophical dialectic is easily perceived as unproductive pedantry.

Nonetheless, equating utility exclusively with technical capability represents a profound intellectual myopia. While science delineates what is technologically feasible, philosophy—specifically the domains of normative ethics, epistemology, and political theory—adjudicates what is morally permissible and socially desirable. For instance, the advent of autonomous weaponry, CRISPR gene editing, and artificial general intelligence does not merely present engineering challenges; it poses profound ontological and normative questions regarding consciousness, moral agency, and justice. Without robust philosophical rigor, technological progress risks degenerating into an unguided mechanism devoid of ethical orientation.

In conclusion, philosophy and science do not exist in an antagonistic dichotomy; rather, they are symbiotic pillars of human civilization. Philosophy provides the critical epistemological foundation and normative compass without which technological mastery becomes perilously rudderless.
